cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Admit You’re Hurt
cards.instruction: Get someone to admit hurt, fear, or disappointment before you reveal that you feel it too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll draft our reply to the boss. Did being called office furniture hurt you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Are you putting my name on a complaint?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not without you reading it. Tell me how it felt first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Invisible. I've worked here twelve years.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Me too. Read this before I send it: 'I went home and cried.'

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 directs drafting; A3 protects B control over attribution to secure a feeling answer; A5 reveals matching pain only after B4 and invites B to read the actual wording.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 naming concern is answered by A3 reading condition; A5 asks for that reading before sending, without assuming B approved.

relationship.evidence: B2 fears exposure in a complaint and B4 explains hurt after long service.

heightening.evidence: B4 invisibility leads A5 from a formal reply to a personal confession of tears that B can inspect.

specificity.evidence: A1 boss insult and B2 joint complaint establish the workplace stakes; B4 twelve years sharpens the injury.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 me too and the draft-reading request combine the admission with the practical next step, without narrating a lesson.
